title: Suggested Apps
lede: The stack I actually reach for. Not a listicle — a short why for each tool, from training runs to shipping MCP servers.

items.name: Cursor
items.why: The editor I use to keep a file-based codebase moving: agents on the boring refactors, me on the architecture.

items.name: Python 3
items.why: Still the shortest path from a messy CSV to a model that a clinician or an intern can rerun.

items.name: TensorFlow / Keras
items.why: What I use when a waveform model has to leave the notebook and sit behind a live inference path.

items.name: scikit-learn
items.why: Baselines first. If XGBoost or a linear model already answers the question, I do not start a neural net.

items.name: Pandas + Polars
items.why: Cleaning is the job. Pandas for the audit trail, Polars when the frame outgrows memory politeness.

items.name: FastAPI
items.why: Typed Python APIs with OpenAPI for free. The audit tool and most of my model wrappers live here.

items.name: LangGraph
items.why: Graphs beat prompt spaghetti when an agent must inspect a repo, call tools, and stop.

items.name: Model Context Protocol
items.why: The contract I am implementing at Zelora: tools with schemas, not hidden side effects.

items.name: Hugging Face
items.why: Weights, datasets, and eval cards in one place. I use it when a paper weight is the starting point, not the finish.

items.name: Weights & Biases
items.why: If I cannot compare two runs, I do not trust the “improvement”.

items.name: Power BI
items.why: When the audience is an operations team, a dashboard they already know beats a custom React chart.

items.name: GitHub
items.why: Source of truth for Cognivus, the audit tool, RepoDigest, and this atlas.
